### Summary

This section keeps the selector, the grid and work-mode gates and the registered arms of the corrected face
work; the derivation of the corrected potential energy, the centroid slope and the implicit row is in
@sec-ch06-dwork and is not repeated here.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects corrected potential-energy work, @eq-ch06-dwork-d.

**Data.** Radial density increment and grid faces in; energy increment out.

**Placement.** Gravity-work bookkeeping and the matching implicit operator.

**Activation.** `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`, default on; requires face work. Not switchable off on a
declared stretched $x_1$ with a `cp3`, `cp5` or `weno5` vertical.

**Guarantee / limits.** Corrected budget on supported measures; unsupported grids warn and fall back; a stretched
$x_1$ deck that switches it off is refused, not degraded.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-radial-exact-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal E = \sum_i V_i E_i + P$ is the corrected domain-integrated energy budget [J],
where $E_i$ is gas energy density [J m$^{-3}$], $V_i$[^rg-861cdfd13eb4] is cell volume [m$^3$] and $P$[^rg-859e2d0bb890] is corrected potential
energy [J]; $g_1$ is radial acceleration [m s$^{-2}$].

### Derivation

See @sec-ch06-dwork for the corrected potential energy and the matching work. The chapter's check line `[C5]`
re-derives the cell-by-cell cancellation of the slope term for a fixed linear slope matrix
[check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

`HydroImpl::gravity_work_radial_exact` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::gravity_work_radial_exact >}})
reads the variable once; `HydroImpl::radial_exact_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}})
adds the three run-time gates: nonzero `grav1`, `gravity-work` equal to `face`, and a grid whose `x1_measure`
({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp x1_measure >}}) is not `none`, which holds for `cartesian`,
`spherical-polar` and `gnomonic-equiangle`. At setup `HydroImpl::reset` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}})
warns once when the switch is on with face work on a grid without a measure and once on a periodic $x_1$
column; neither warning changes the run. In `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}})
the corrected work replaces the curvature work of the `cp3`, `cp5` and `weno5` faces rather than adding to it,
books the increment with `corrected_pe_work` ({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp corrected_pe_work >}})
on an unsplit column, and with `corrected_pe_work_seam`
({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp corrected_pe_work_seam >}}) across an $x_1$ seam, where the
neighbour's density change is exchanged so that a seam cell takes the centred slope of one block; a periodic
$x_1$ column keeps the one-sided slope at its block edges. With `face-wallc` the $x_1$ wall cells keep the cell
work. An implicit scheme refuses an $x_1$ split, so the implicit row sees one block
(`HydroImpl::face_work_in_operator`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::face_work_in_operator >}}). The
YAML default `gravity-work: face` is set by `ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

### Code

**How to use it.** Set `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=1` explicitly before launch for a corrected-budget run.
Merge this fragment into a complete card with non-periodic radial boundaries:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `gravity-work-fixer`[^rg-a5b993b32d10].
```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8     # m s^-2
    gravity-work: face
    gravity-work-fixer: false
```

Use a fresh process with RE=0 for the plain-budget control. Periodic radial boundaries and unsupported measures
produce warnings, not refusals; they do not establish the corrected-budget guarantee. The separate implicit
operator refuses a radial block split (@sec-ch12-matrix).

**The one case where the control is not available.** On a grid that declares a stretched $x_1$
(`geometry/x1f` or `geometry/cells/x1rat`) with a `cp3`, `cp5` or `weno5` vertical reconstruction, switching this
off does not give the plain face form: the stage then reaches the $\tfrac{\Delta x_1^2}{12}$ curvature flux,
which has no correct two-point form on unequal cells, and throws
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}; the message and the ways out are in
@sec-ch06-face). The plain-budget control on such a grid therefore needs `gravity-work: cell` instead of
`RE=0`, which changes the scheme and not only the switch.

`HydroImpl::radial_exact_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}) contains this selection step:

```cpp
  return gravity_work_radial_exact() && g && g->grav1() != 0. &&
         g->gravity_work() == "face" && x1_measure(type) != X1Measure::none;
```

All four predicates must hold before the work in @eq-ch06-dwork-d is selected. `[C5]` checks its algebraic
cancellation for a fixed linear slope operator; it does not execute this C++ branch.

: Implementation sites for the corrected-work selector. {#tbl-ch12-radial-exact-code}

1. Read the switch once; combine it with the gravity, work-mode and measure gates. The anchor
   `radial_exact_work` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}.
2. At setup, warn once on a grid without a measure and on a periodic $x_1$ column. The anchor
   `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}.
3. Book the corrected increment instead of the curvature work, with the seam form on a split column. The
   anchor `radial_exact` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
On a declared stretched $x_1$ with a five-point vertical, this switch cannot be turned off without changing
`gravity-work`, so the registered off arms do not cover that grid, and the "fourth order there" the refusal
message claims for this scheme on a stretched grid is not fitted by any test at the pin (@sec-ch06-dwork,
Limits item 5). A grid without an $x_1$ measure keeps the first-order plain face work with only a warning. A lone
gnomonic-equiangle block with reflecting lateral walls is a mass-conservation question of the grid, not of this
switch (@sec-ch16). Split and unsplit $x_1$ columns agree except on a periodic $x_1$ column, whose seams keep
the one-sided slope.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-861cdfd13eb4]: $V_i$ — cell volume

[^rg-859e2d0bb890]: $P$ — corrected discrete potential energy $\sum_iV_i[\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]]$, exact to $O(h^4)$

[^rg-a5b993b32d10]: gravity-work-fixer — whether the gravity-work fixer runs (a boolean; default true with `gravity-work: cell`, and it needs `cell`)

[^rg-3ec07417d3f2]: $\mathcal E$ — the conserved energy functional of a scheme, named each time ($\mathcal E = \sum_iV_iE_i+P$ under D, $\sum_iV_iE_i+\mathrm{PE}_d$ under the plain face form)

[^rg-7da3ad6259c0]: VIC — vertically implicit correction
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
